Allergies:
No Known Allergies / Adverse Drug Reactions

Chief Complaint:
Fall

History of Present Illness:
This is an ___ man with history of hypertension, chronic 
venous insufficiency and ? Afib who presents as a transfer from 
outside hospital after a fall, with small traumatic subarachnoid 
hemorrhage and possible C5-C6 fracture secondary to lesion.

Patient states he was at home, where he lives alone, and was 
ambulating with his walker when his knees buckled, and he fell 
backwards, hitting his head on a piece of furniture. He has 
known OA and he has fallen before due to the same reason. He 
denies loss of consciousness. He was unable to get up for 1 hour 
at
which point he called his son, who came to help him up. They 
called EMS, who transported him to outside hospital. 

At outside hospital, he had a head CT concerning for a small 
parietal subarachnoid hemorrhage, and a CT of the neck showing a 
possible C5-C6 fracture versus neoplastic process. He was also 
noted to have a scalp hematoma. Labs were notable for elevated 
BNP. Patient notes that for the past 3 days he has had a cough, 
and 2 days ago he had a low-grade fever to ___ F. He has
otherwise been well. Denies chest pain, shortness of breath, 
orthopnea, abdominal pain, vomiting, diarrhea, dysuria, 
hematuria. He has chronic lower extremity edema that has not 
been worsening.

At OSH, he was also noted to be in atrial fibrillation, rate 
controlled. Patient reports that his doctors have mentioned A 
fib to him in the past but doesn't recall if he was treated for 
it. He also reports that he was on a 'yellow blood thinner' at 
some point in the past.

In the ED, his VSS notable for BP of 199/79. He was awake and 
alert, no acute distress. In c-collar. Hematoma and laceration 
to occiput, no active bleeding. Neuro exam nonfocal. No chest 
wall tenderness to palpation or crepitus. Abdomen soft and 
nontender. Abrasion to right paraspinal region. No midline T or 
L-spine
tenderness to palpation.

His labs notable for:
Na 133
AST 62, ALT 42, INR 1.4
___ 12922
Trops neg

Imaging studies as follows:
CT C spine notable for acute kyphosis, lucent involvement of the
posterior arch of C5 and C6 involving the facets bilaterally,
cannot exclude acute fracture, severe bone loss involving the
vertebral body of C6, which may represent a neoplastic process
and a small subgaleal hematoma along the right posterior 
occiput.

CT abdomen/ pelvis notable for bilateral small pleural 
effusions,
with ground-glass opacities in the lungs bilaterally suggestive
of pulmonary edema, cholelithiasis and enlarged prostate.

Patient was given:
Atenolol 100mg
Allopurinol ___
Losartan 100mg
Furosemide 40mg IV x1

Upon arrival to the floor, patient collaborates the story above.
He has mild throbbing pain at the laceration site but no other
concerns. 

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS:

Complete ROS obtained and is otherwise negative.

Brief Hospital Course:
This is an ___ man with history of hypertension, chronic 
venous insufficiency and Afib who presents as a transfer from 
outside hospital after a fall, with small traumatic subarachnoid 
hemorrhage and C5-C6 fracture concerning for underlying 
malignancy, also presenting with CHF exacerbation.

ACUTE ISSUES:
=============
#C5-C6 mass, fracture 
Patient presented from OSH after unwitnessed fall, was noted to 
have a C5-6 fracture on CT spine concerning for a malignant 
process, possibly multiple myeloma; MRI obtained on ___, 
demonstrating mass extending into spinal cord. He was maintained 
in a cervical collar throughout admission. Neurosurgery followed 
the patient, and recommended an ___ biopsy of the mass, 
which took place on ___ and pathology consistent with chordoma. 
CT Abd/Pelvis was obtained to look for any evidence of any 
primary malignant process, but was unrevealing with the 
exception of a possible small pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor 
and adrenal nodule, neither of which was thought to be likely 
related to his spinal mass. Neurosurgery proceeded with full 
resection on ___. He was transferred to the ___ under the 
Neurosurgery service for close monitoring. Following his 
surgery, he was noted to be weaker on the right side, only 
withdrawing his right arm/leg. Post-operative CT C-Spine showed 
intact hardware.  A CTA head/neck was done that was negative for 
acute stroke. On POD#2, his anterior and posterior JP drains 
were removed. Post-pull XR was stable. A NCHCT was again ordered 
on ___ for his persistent right-sided weakness and diminished 
movement, which was negative for acute stroke. On ___, the 
patient continued with the right upper and lower extremity 
weakness which was worsening from prior documentation. A CT of 
the cervical spine, CT head and MRI of the brain were ordered 
for further evaluation of the weakness. CTH was negative for any 
acute process and was stable compared to prior imaging. Again 
the brain MRI revealed a subacute infarct in the left corona 
radiata, left basal ganglia, and left insula with associated 
cortical laminar necrosis as well as a subacute right cerebellar 
infarct. MRI also showed Foci of intraparenchymal hemorrhage in 
the right parietal lobe, right corona radiata, and left basal 
ganglia and insula. Patient's Cspine CT was notable for 
prevertebral edema as well as a fluid collection which slight 
deviates the trachea leftward however patient's respiratory 
status has remained stable. On ___ patient was ordered for an 
MRI cspine with a without contrast for better visualization and 
revealed no acute complication. His strength was slowly slightly 
improving on right. 

#Left M1 thrombus s/p thrombectomy with TICI III reperfusion on 
___.
Etiology presumed cardio-embolic in setting of afib not on A/C. 
NIHSS18 pre-thrombectomy 18 and 2 24 hours after thrombectomy. 
CTH at 24 hours stable. Started on aspirin 81 mg but was held in 
anticipation of spinal surgery the following week. Home 
atorvastatin 40 mg daily was continued. SBP goal <160 given 
individualized assessment of adequate collateralization. He is 
being monitored on telemetry. Stroke risk factors reveal A1c: 
7.7, LDL: 40. TTE with Mild regional left ventricular systolic 
dysfunction, c/w CAD; Mild mitral and aortic regurgitation; The 
patient appears to be in atrial fibrillation. He initially 
failed swallow study and was NPO receiving TF, eventually his 
diet was able to be advanced. In setting of new stroke, spinal 
surgery should be deferred for at least 1 week after stroke. 
Aspirin will be held, and no anticoagulation was started due to 
bleeding risk at first. However after we demonstrated by 
clinical and radiographic stability, he was started on an 
heparin drip on ___ for stroke prevention while awaiting 
surgery. After his operation, he should be started on Apixaban 
5mg BID when able from a surgical standpoint. He was initiated 
on ASA 81mg daily on ___ for stroke prophylaxis. He developed 
RUE weakness, R facial and slurred speech on ___ and code 
stroke was activated. CTA showed known infarcts with no vessel 
occlusion. His exam returned to baseline. Eliquis was started on 
___.

#Dysphagia 
Patient with swallowing difficulty and remained on TF with the 
NGT. SLP continued to follow patient throughout hospital stay 
and continued to make recommendations. He continued to fail 
swallow evaluation and PEG was recommended. ACS was initially 
consulted for PEG placement however it was deferred to ___ given 
recent spinal surgery. He went to ___ for PEG ___. Tube feeds 
were resumed and well tolerated. 

#Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction
Patient presented with ___ edema, CXR/Chest CT suggestive of 
fluid overload, and elevated ___ at 12922, concerning for a 
new diagnosis of congestive heart failure. Etiology of CHF 
includes ACS vs infection vs arrhythmia. Trop x1 at OSH neg and 
repeat here also neg. EKG initially with biphasic T waves and 
repeat
with diffuse TWI c/f Wellens vs cerebral T waves. Pt also had 
SBPs in the 190s, as well as A fib whilst in the ED, which could 
both be contributing factors to his HF. He was diuresed with IV 
Lasix for several days, and was mainatined on losartan 100mg QD, 
amlodipine 10mg, and hydralazine PRN for afterload reduction. He 
was also started on carvedilol 25mg BID for neuro-hormonal 
blockade (had been on labetalol at home). TTE was performed, 
showed a newly reduced EF of 45-50% with inferior wall 
abnormalities. Cardiac catheterization was strongly considered 
to look for reversible occlusion, but would require heparin 
bolus; this was deferred in setting of SAH (see below), and 
ultimately deferred as malignancy workup was pursued, as above. 

#Nutrition
Following his OR procedure on ___, he was made NPO. SLP 
evaluated him on ___ and maintained his NPO status. He had a 
NGT in place, and his pre-operative tube feeds were resumed on 
___. SLP continued to evaluate patient throughout hospital 
stay. Banana flakes added for loose stool. 

#Fall
#Subarachnoid Hemorrhage
Patient presented from OSH after unwitnessed fall due to his 
knee buckling, with head strike and laceration on scalp with 2 
staples. His neuro exam has been reassuringly nonfocal. Imaging 
studies notable for small SAH at OSH CT head, no intervention 
required per neurosurgery; patient should follow up in ___ 
clinic as needed. Neurosurgery recommended against starting an 
antiepileptic. Blood pressure was controlled as documented 
below, with goal SBP < 160. 

#A fib
CHADSVASC=5. Patient was in A fib at OSH, but rate-controlled. 
He appears to have only recently been diagnosed with Afib, at a 
PCP appointment within the last year (captured on EKG). Was not 
on anticoagulation on admission. He was maintained on rate 
control, transitioned to carvedilol, and was monitired on 
telemetry. Anticoagulation was held given plans to operative 
intervention of his spinal mass, as above. 

#Anemia
Hg 12.12 at OSH and 12.4 here, ultimately stabilized in the 
10.9-11 range.
Unclear what his baseline hemoglobin is. Iron studies consistent 
with anemia of chronic disease. 

#EKG changes
No baseline EKG on file, but initial EKG in the ED showed 
biphasic T
waves in V2-V3 and QTc at 519. Repeat EKG showing in V1-V6, II,
III and aVf. Differential included cerebral T waves in the 
setting of
SAH. Discussed with cardiology fellow, as above, who recommended 
monitoring. Repeat EKG on ___ reassuring, less prominent ST and 
T changes, although TWI in anterolateral leads still evident.  
Reassuringly, patient was asymptomatic, with negative troponins. 
TTE ultimated showed evidence of inferior WMA. He had a negative 
stress test.  

#Hypertension
Patient had severe hypertension in the ED to 190s, in the 
setting
of holding his home meds. He then received his home atenolol and
losartan, but his SBP was still in the 180s. He remained
asymptomatic throughout. BPs came down in 1 day, to SBP in the 
160 range. His labetaolol was transitioned to carvedilol 25mg 
BID, home losartan 100mg was continued, and he was started on 
amlodipine 10mg daily. PRN hydralazone was also ordered, to 
maintain SBP<160. Patient had been on both an ACEi and ___ at 
home; ACEi was discontinued. 

#Sacral wounds
A 0.5x0.5 unstagable pressure ulcer was noted in the sacral area 
on admission; wound care team followed and made recommendations 
with regard to appropriate care. 

#Hematuria
On ___, the patient was noted to have blood in his urine. A 
urinalysis was sent which appeared negative. On ___ patient was 
noted to have blood clots in the foley bag, urology was 
consulted and believed that this was likely related to trauma 
and irritation of the foley. Patient's UOP continued to be 
monitored closely and improved.

#loose stool 
Patient was noted to have multiple loose stools. A cdiff PCR was 
sent and resulted as positive on ___. Patient was started on 
antibioitcs (PO vancomycin) for a total of 4 days when the toxin 
antigen assay resulted as negative.  

#Balanitis
Patient noted to have swollen penis and was evaluated by 
urology. Recommended conservative treatment with saline cleanse 
BID and monitoring with hydrocortisone cream if no improvement.

#UTI
Urine culture grew EColi and he was given CTX x1 then started 
cipro x1 week after sensitivities resulted. Foley catheter was 
changed ___.

CHRONIC ISSUES:
===============
#DM
- Held metformin while inpatient; maintained on ISS. Glargine 
was initiated on ___ starting with 6units QHS. ___ was 
consulted for diabetic management and made adjustments to 
insulin regimen as needed. 

#BPH
- Continued Tamsulosin

# Gout
- Continued allopurinol

# Glaucoma 
- Continued home eye drops 

TRANSITIONAL ISSUES:
==================
[ ] Alterations made to home blood pressure medication regimen 
[ ] Elevated free kappa
[ ] NET, adrenal nodule, renal cyst on CT Abd/Pel
[ ] Pulmonary nodules on CT scan
[ ] Anti-coagulation discussion for afib

AHA/ASA Core Measures for Ischemic Stroke and Transient Ischemic 
Attack  
1. Dysphagia screening before any PO intake? (x) Yes, confirmed 
done 
2. DVT Prophylaxis administered? (x) Yes
3. Antithrombotic therapy administered by end of hospital day 2? 
(x) No. bleeding risk
4. LDL documented? (x) Yes (LDL = 40 ) 
5. Intensive statin therapy administered? atorvastatin 40mg  
6. Smoking cessation counseling given? (x) non-smoker   
7. Stroke education (personal modifiable risk factors, how to 
activate EMS for stroke, stroke warning signs and symptoms, 
prescribed medications, need for followup) given in written 
form? (x) Yes 
8. Assessment for rehabilitation or rehab services considered? 
(x) Yes 
9. Discharged on statin therapy? (x) Yes 
10. Discharged on antithrombotic therapy? (x) Yes [Type: (x) 
Antiplatelet - (x) Anticoagulation] 
11. Discharged on oral anticoagulation for patients with atrial 
fibrillation/flutter? (x) Yes

Discharge Diagnosis:
PRIMARY DIAGNOSIS
=================
C5-C6 mass
Subarachnoid hemorrhage
Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction

SECONDARY DIAGNOSIS
==================
Atrial fibrillation
Chronic venous stasis
